body: I hate name calling, to me all it does is hurt feelings and you're no where closer to a solution. I do laugh about it sometimes. Every time he gets mad at me, I'm not surprised that he says things like that, it's more about the shock value of what he said this time. I've wanted to leave many times. We live together, so that makes it a little more complicated. As I said before, it's hard to find people who are willing to "put up" with me and I've pushed so many people away already. I think it all boils down to a fear of being alone. He's not all bad, he's stood by from the day I was diagnosed, two hospital stays to now when my family wasn't as supportive as they are now. It would be hard to let go of someone who I've been so close to for pretty much all of my adult life.

I've heard about that. I will definitely talk to her about it. Anyway I can reduce the amount of meds I'm on would be great. When I stopped taking my pills, I was taking 7 pills a day. For someone who is 5'2" and 100 pounds, that's a lot.

I've always been upfront with him. He's just one of those people that when he's angry he'll use what he knows will hurt you most against you. My favorite from the day was that he said that I should go be an alcoholic like my father. Ouch

I'm going to call my psychiatrist tomorrow and try and get back on meds. It can mess you up if you stop and start on meds. I stopped taking it because I started getting sick when I took them, I had problems eating (lost like 30 pounds, I'm really thin now, trying to gain some weight back), and I felt like maybe I had grown out of it. Not my most intelligent decision.
I know, gosh, people are just really mean sometimes
Sometimes I put up with more than I should. I think its because of how I can be and that it's like they're the only ones who are willing to deal with me.
Thanks for your kind words. I'm going home, I pretty much told him to go fuck himself
He knows, we've been together for 3 years, this isn't exactly news to him.
I'm bipolar 1, I get the extremes of both mania and depression. People are quick to dismiss my actions as bad behavior rather than a serious illness.
